endorsements.quote: The implementation of clinical AI in radiology requires strong leadership and robust governance frameworks to oversee not only algorithm evaluation, selection and deployment, but also ongoing maintenance through transparent performance monitoring, automated quality controls, and regular retraining [ 17, 21].

The implementation of clinical AI in radiology requires strong leadership and robust governance frameworks to oversee not only algorithm evaluation, selection and deployment, but also ongoing maintenance through transparent performance monitoring, automated quality controls, and regular retraining [ 17, 21].

To ensure adherence to ethical principles and appropriate supervision of the implementation, maintenance, and monitoring of AI algorithms, establishing sound governance and organizational frameworks will be essential [ 17, 29].
Implementing AI initiatives will drive organizational change that needs to be successfully managed and requires significant financial investment, not just in technology, but also in human capital.

unlisted_practices: Radiology leaders should ensure AI enhances rather than replaces the role and skills of radiology professionals.
Radiology leaders should develop understanding of AI concepts and the human, administrative, and organizational challenges of AI implementation.
Radiology leaders should build institution-wide buy-in and cross-departmental and cross-disciplinary partnerships for AI adoption.
Radiology leaders should foster a culture of continuous learning and diversity through tailored curricula, mentoring, and coaching.
